draft.shortGloss: to lose; to misplace; to get rid of
draft.emotion: frustrated and slightly frantic, like patting down all your pockets
notes: Godan (group 1) transitive verb (also written 無くす). Its intransitive pair is なくなる (to get lost; to disappear; to run out): 鍵をなくした (I lost my keys) vs. 鍵がなくなった (my keys are gone).
For people or animals going missing, use いなくなる rather than なくす.

senses.definition: To misplace something or no longer have it.

examples.text: どこかで鍵をなくしてしまった。

senses.definition: To get rid of or remove something unwanted.

examples.text: 時間の無駄をなくしたい。
examples.translation: I want to eliminate wasted time.

draftBefore.emotion: frustrated and slightly frantic, like patting down all your pockets
notes: Use なくす for items you have misplaced or lost. It implies the item still exists somewhere, but you cannot find it.
Do not confuse this with いなくなる (to go missing/disappear), which is used for people or pets.

senses.definition: To not know where something is any more because you have misplaced it.

examples.emotion: annoyed and regretful, realizing the keys are gone
examples.note: Past tense of なくす is なくした.

senses.definition: To get rid of or eliminate something.

examples.emotion: determined and professional, focusing on efficiency

faults.why: Overstated: なくす covers Sense 1 (eliminating) and losing abstract things like confidence.
